To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a population of ventrolateral premotor neurons play a role during the planning and execution of goal‐directed actions.
the VLPFC contains neurons that are involved in the control of goal‐directed actions, and that these neurons are not involved in the selection of abstract rules.
the monkey ventrolate prefrontal cortex contains neurons active during grasping movements, and some of them respond also to object presentation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the neural basis of goal‐directed action, and more specifically with the role of the pre‐motor and pre‐frontal cortex in action control and planning.
the neural mechanisms underlying action planning and control.
the functional role of prefrontal cortex during goal‐directing hand actions in different contextual situations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the VLPP cortex is involved in the control of goal‐directed actions, but its role seems to be that of a coordinator of action execution, rather than that of an action planner.
the VLPC plays a role in the control of grasping actions in a number of contexts.
the prefrontal cortical areas are not involved in motor control per se, but in the selection of the motor act to be performed on the basis of the contextual conditions of the situation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VLPF movement related neurons play a role during goal directed actions.

the VLPFC movement‐related neurons are not involved in the selection and control of abstract rules, but rather in the selection of the motor goal and the execution of goal‐directed actions in a wide variety of contextual conditions, including the absence of abstract rule.
the VLPPFC is involved in the control of goal‐directed actions, and this is done through the integration of information about the motor goal and the context in which the action is performed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prefrontal movement‐related neurons play a role not only in planning but also in the execution of goal‐directed actions, in different contexts.
the VLPC plays a role in controlling the goal of an action, rather than the motor plan per se.

the prefrontal movement‐related neurons play a role not only in controlling action execution in the absence of visual feedback but also in guiding action execution on the grounds of contextual information.
